title: Performance fingerprinting + pinning playbook for hybrid quantized and variant model onboarding
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Goal: Create a repeatable, observable playbook to produce a compact "performance fingerprint" for newly ingested model variants (including FP16, int8, hybrid-quant, and sparsified builds), use that fingerprint to drive deterministic pin decisions, and automate publishing of performance profiles to the model catalog and docs. This is intended to reduce manual gating time and ensure reliable runtime behavior across Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments.

Scope:
- Microbenchmark harness and required sample workloads (generation: 8/32/1024 tokens; chat-turns; embeddings; reranking) across seq-len percentiles.
- Measurements collected: median & p95/p99 latency, token/sec throughput, peak GPU memory, warm vs cold KV cache behavior, decoding cost-per-token estimates, and deterministic quality checks (a small eval suite).
- Canonical "performance fingerprint" artifact format: compact tag + vector of normalized metrics + SDK-friendly URL to raw perf bundle.
- Pinning policy: automated delta thresholds (e.g., latency regression >5% OR quality drop >2% triggers hold), stable fingerprint hash for immutable pins, and fallback mapping for deprecated variants.
- Publish flow: automated performance-signature publish to catalog + auto-generate docs snippet (examples for Console and API pages) + mark variant as "canary" for 24h traffic ramp in staging before GA publish.

Deliverables:
1) Benchmark harness and CI job that runs ingest-time perf collection and produces a performance fingerprint JSON.
2) Validation step that computes delta vs baseline and emits a human-readable summary + pass/fail.
3) Catalog ingestion pipeline change to store fingerprint metadata and pin-status fields.
4) Docs templates and console UI copy & example queries for new catalog entries.
5) Runbook for SRE/Oncall when a pinned variant regresses in production.

Tradeoffs and decisions so far:
- We prioritize latency/throughput and memory over exhaustive quality evaluation at onboarding time to keep CI runtime short; a secondary nightly quality eval will run on broader eval sets.
- Hybrid-quant variants require additional wall-time for multiple sequence lengths; to keep runtime reasonable we sample three representative seq lengths (8, 128, 1024) and extrapolate middle percentiles. This is acceptable for pinning heuristics but flagged in the fingerprint metadata.
- Deterministic fingerprint format chosen to be compact for storage but with links to full perf bundles for debugging.

Open questions:
- Exact numerical thresholds for automatic pin-hold vs. auto-rollback. Proposal: latency regressions >5% or token-efficiency drop >7% -> block automatic pin; quality drop >2% -> require manual sign-off. Need PM + SRE sign-off.
- Do we surface raw perf bundles in Private deployments by default or gate to approved users? Security team to advise.

Next steps:
- Finish benchmark harness PR and CI (owner: Marcus Li).
- Draft concise docs snippet for Console and API (owner: Sofia Patel, Design review pending).
- Run onboarding on 3 representative open-source models as proof-of-concept and collect baseline artifacts (owner: Avery Chen).

Notes on compatibility:
- Fingerprint schema will be backward-compatible: new optional fields appended, and a schema version number embedded.
- The catalog UI will show a short "perf badge" and link to full metrics; Console engineers should be given a JSON sample to wire the UI card.

Expected timeline: PoC perf fingerprints in 10 business days, catalog ingestion changes merged within the following sprint, docs + console changes staged for release with runtime-1.22.
